correctness.rationale: The full line/parallel-class classification, pair-trace relation, first-order point and incidence definitions, order-two obstruction and consequent automorphism identification are the exact claim assessed. The inequalities \(p(q+1)+\ell\ge q(q+1)\) and \(p+q\ell\ge q^2\) imply \(p=q\) and \(\ell=q-1\) at the \(2q-1\) threshold. Equality forces \(q-1\) parallel lines and their missing line of \(q\) chosen points. Pair witnesses and four triple-type obstructions prove the complete trace classification; all root positive children have dimension at most one, while a shattered pair gives dimension two. The first-order predicate characterizes point vertices via their independent nonneighbors, and mixed nonadjacency recovers original incidence for \(q\ge3\). Python orders two, three, four, five and C++ orders two, three, five, seven verify finite traces, with optimum-set exhaustive checks at orders two and three; those checks are not used to replace the unrestricted proof.

value.rationale: The finite-model-theoretic reconstruction of the entire sorted plane from a definable two-query extremal trace relation is structural, natural and uniform in all finite affine planes, including non-Desarguesian cases. A sharp order-two definability failure, full shattering polynomial, exact online dimension and integral topological classification make a coherent all-order theorem rather than a routine parameter recomputation.
